hero.name: Elina Mosoian
hero.tagline: Breaking things (on purpose) to learn how to defend them.
hero.intro: Third-year cybersecurity student focused on network defense, offensive security fundamentals, and secure application design. I build labs, break my own code, and write up what I learn.

about.heading: About
paragraphs: I'm a cybersecurity student who got into this field after setting up a home lab just to see if I could break it. That curiosity turned into a habit of building vulnerable environments, patching them, and documenting the process.

My focus areas right now are network security, Linux hardening, and web application security. I'm working toward a career in security operations or penetration testing, and I spend a lot of my free time on CTFs and personal security tooling.

projects.title: Home Lab SIEM
projects.description: A self-hosted Security Information and Event Management setup using the Elastic stack, ingesting logs from a small virtualized network to practice detection engineering.

projects.title: Intentionally Vulnerable Web App
projects.description: A deliberately vulnerable Flask application built to practice and teach OWASP Top 10 exploitation and remediation, complete with writeups for each vulnerability class.

projects.title: Async Network Scanner
projects.description: A lightweight asynchronous port and service scanner written in Python, built as a faster learning alternative to understand how tools like nmap work under the hood.

projects.title: Phishing Awareness Simulator
projects.description: A campus club project: a controlled phishing simulation platform used to run authorized awareness campaigns and generate reporting-rate analytics for student orgs.

timeline.title: B.S. Cybersecurity
timeline.description: Coursework in network security, applied cryptography, and systems administration. Active member of the Cyber Defense Club.

timeline.title: Security Operations Intern
timeline.description: Monitored SIEM alerts, triaged phishing reports, and assisted with quarterly vulnerability scans across client environments.

timeline.title: Cyber Defense Club — CTF Team Lead
timeline.description: Organize weekly CTF practice sessions and represent the university at regional collegiate cybersecurity competitions.

timeline.title: High School Diploma
timeline.description: Graduated with honors; led the introductory coding club and completed an independent study in networking fundamentals.
